memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then God said, "Take your son, your only son, whom you love - Isaac - and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you." - Gen 22:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is perhaps the most staggering command in all of Scripture. God asks Abraham to sacrifice Isaac - the son he waited twenty-five years for, the son of the promise, the son through whom all God's covenant blessings were to come. And notice how God words it, each phrase pressing on Abraham's heart: "your son, your only son, whom you love - Isaac." God names exactly what He is asking Abraham to surrender.

We must sit honestly with how hard this is. This is not a small ask. It touches the deepest love of Abraham's heart and seems to contradict the very promise God had made. How could the promise be fulfilled through Isaac if Isaac were dead? The command appears to collide with everything God had said.

We should also be clear: God never intended for Abraham to actually kill Isaac, and Scripture is emphatic elsewhere that God detests child sacrifice (Jer 32:35). This was a test of Abraham's heart, and God would provide another way, as we'll see. But Abraham did not yet know that. For him, the command was real and total.

There is something here about the cost of following God. Sometimes He touches the very thing we love most and asks, "Do you trust Me even with this?" These are the hardest moments of faith. Yet Abraham's story assures us that God can be trusted even when His call seems to cost us everything - because the God who asks is the same God who provides.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there something you love most that God is asking you to hold with open hands?
- Can you trust God even when His call seems to cost you everything?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You sometimes touch the thing I love most and ask if I trust You even with that. Give me a heart that holds everything with open hands, trusting that the God who asks is the God who provides.
Amen.
